fixtures.label: Flat per-unit levy on a zero-priced component
fixtures.description: Renders 7 columns. The only fixture carrying a `flat` (per-unit) TAX, and the reason `hide_zero_priced_components` can work on an invoice at all. The param's predicate is `zero_priced === true && componentDepth > 0`, the same question `quote.eta` asks. ⚠️ It keyed on `price.base_cents === 0` until 2026-09-10, because an invoice line genuinely had no `zero_priced` field until stage two of manager#421 backfilled the corpus and made the projection emit. This document proves that predicate finds the right row: 10 cases of water carry a zero-priced `Bottled Water ( /bottle )` child at 24 bottles each, and the Water Bottle Tax bills 240 x $0.05 = $12.00 against a $0.00 subtotal, beside 10.5% Chicago Sales Tax on the $390.00 parent. The flat arm reads QUANTITY and ignores subtotal, so it is the one branch that can put real money on a line whose Unit Price and Subtotal are both $0.00 — which is what the em-dash cell rule exists for: an em-dash says the value was computed and is nothing, where a blank reads as missing data. With the param ON the row hides and its $12.00 must roll onto the parent (Tax $40.95 -> $52.95, Total $430.95 -> $442.95) while #totals still reads $442.95, so the grid reconciles with its own footer instead of losing the money. It is also the family's only COMPONENT fixture: the child sits at path depth 5 under the three-level `[order, destination, group]` hierarchy and resolves to component depth 1, proving `componentDepth` counts line-item ancestors rather than subtracting a fixed number of divider levels. Captured from prod invoice 2390, the invoice for order 1004 — the same order behind the quote family's `taxed-zero-priced-component`, so the two families can be compared on one document. Measured 2026-08-26, order 1004 is still the only one of 997 prod orders carrying a flat tax, so if this fixture is dropped do not assume a replacement is available.

fixtures.label: Partly paid — a real Amount Due
fixtures.description: The only fixture with a NON-ZERO Amount Due, and therefore the only one where the settlement block says something a quote never can. $196.25 paid against $306.50, leaving $110.25 outstanding, at status `part_paid`. Settlement is the invoice's whole reason for existing as a separate family, and it is unreachable in detail: `Invoice.payments[]` was deleted 2026-08-03 and `InvoiceSchema` is a `z.strictObject`, so it cannot come back — the per-settlement journal is a separate `settlements` collection and a template only ever receives `it.doc`. So the document reports ROLLUPS, and this fixture is what pins them rendering correctly. It exercises the two rows that always print (Amount Paid, Amount Due) while leaving Credits Applied ABSENT, which is the other half of the rule: a credits row is omitted entirely at zero, because "$0.00 credited" states an absence as if it were a fact. Pair it with `credits-applied`, which covers the arm where it does print; a template that hard-coded the row would pass on that one alone. Renders 7 columns — tax on, no rental so no Duration, no discount. Captured from prod invoice 2364.

fixtures.label: Credits applied — all three settlement rows
fixtures.description: Renders 7 columns. The only fixture that renders the Credits Applied row, and the only one where all three settlement rows carry a non-zero figure: $399.00 paid, $40.90 credited, against a $439.90 total. `totals.amount_credited_cents` is a bare `.optional()` with NO schema default, so most invoices simply do not have it and every read needs `?? 0` — this is the document that proves the row appears when the field is present, where `part-paid` proves it stays absent when it is not. Those two are a pair and neither substitutes for the other: one covers the conditional being true, the other false, and a template that hard-coded the row would pass on this one alone. Also worth knowing when reading a diff: Amount Due is $0.00 here while the invoice is fully settled, so this is the fixture that shows a zero Amount Due still printing — grand totals are deliberately exempt from the blank-at-zero rule, because a settled balance of zero is a fact about the invoice rather than an absent value. Captured from prod invoice 1252.

fixtures.label: 6-column floor, no destinations block, and a fee that must not be a row
fixtures.description: Renders 6 columns — the FLOOR — and NO #destinations section at all. Three jobs nothing else does. (1) THE FLOOR: one untaxed service line, no rental, no discount — every conditional column off, header exactly Item Description / Type / Qty / Unit Price / Subtotal / Total. (2) THE ABSENT DESTINATIONS TABLE. ⚠️ THIS CLAIM CHANGED 2026-09-08: it previously read that this fixture proved the block collapses its RETURN LEG. That is now false. `hasDeliverableItems` widened from `type !== "replacement"` to `rental` or `sale`, so a service-only invoice drops the WHOLE table. Why: prod invoice 2413 charged $250 to collect 30 Z Racks on 9/9 and printed `In Store Pickup / Tue 6/23/26 / 3100 W Fillmore St` — the June leg on which the customer took them away from OUR OWN warehouse — suppressing the 9/9 date, site address and contact the charge was about. The wrong leg, stated confidently. A STOPGAP that loses a real date: templates#279 holds the measurement and the open decision. Do not narrow the predicate back to shrink this golden. ⚠️ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SET: the half-collapsed shape (`hasCollection` false while the table still renders) is now reachable only on a SALE-only invoice and NOTHING here covers it — this fixture used to, and none is captured. A green run says nothing about that arm. (3) A `transaction_fee` ITEM beside the service line, carried by nothing else here. A fee is stored in `items[]` but is NOT a line of the invoice — priced FROM the document, with `totals.transaction_fees` derived from these very items — so rendering both bills the customer twice. Verified 2026-08-26: the $14.00 Card Fee is in the totals block, NOT the items grid. Expect the Total column not to sum to `totals.total_cents`; the fee is added after the lines. Captured from prod invoice 2353 (order 977), the order behind the quote family's `service-untaxed`. ⚠️ That sibling still renders its block: `quote.eta` was NOT changed, so a service-only quote keeps the defect (templates#279).

fixtures.label: 9-column ceiling, single view
fixtures.description: Renders 9 columns — the CEILING. Duration, Discount and Tax all on at once, which is the widest grid the template can emit and therefore the one that decides whether the money columns still fit under `table-layout: fixed`. Two rentals in one group with a $4.00 discount and an 11% rental tax, on a $50.62 invoice: deliberately the smallest carrier of the shape available, so the whole grid is readable in a single view and a column-width regression is obvious rather than buried. Keep it small — its job is the column combination and nothing else, so do not enrich it with content. The 9-column count is also what puts `--block-3-fraction` at its exact-half value: `addressBoundary = floor((9-1)/2) = 4` of 8 address sub-columns, where the even counts land off-centre. Alongside `service-untaxed-fee` at 6 and the two 8-column fixtures, this brackets the range the shared items-grid partial has to survive — the same 6-to-9 span the quote family covers, rendered from the same partial, which is the point of sharing it. Captured from prod invoice 1902.

fixtures.label: Foreign billing address
fixtures.description: The only fixture whose `organization.billing_address.country_name` is not `United States` — a Canadian address — and therefore the only one that renders the country line in `#bill-to` at all. Every other fixture bills to a US address, so without this the conditional is dead in every golden and a green run says nothing about it. That is not a hypothetical failure mode: on the quote family this same country line, and the flat-tax totals row, were both dead branches that passed every run until a fixture reached them. Deliberately the SMALLEST carrier available at $146.52, so the golden diff shows the address block and little else. Its 8-column Duration + Tax grid is incidental rather than its job — but it is nonetheless the family's ONLY carrier of that shape, which is the commonest thing production writes, so do not delete it as a near-duplicate of the address coverage: `rental-discount-untaxed` holds the other 8-column shape (Duration + Discount) and neither substitutes. Measured 2026-08-26 by rendering the set. It carries a SECOND coverage argument now that api-cloudrun#627 has landed: it is the family's only non-US postcode, so it is the only one exercising the shape-preserving postcode mask on a format that is not a US ZIP. Re-captured 2026-09-06 on the corrected masker; the old `Sample t` artifact this description used to warn about is gone. Captured from prod invoice 1918.

fixtures.label: Discount with no Tax column beside it
fixtures.description: 8 columns via Duration + Discount with Tax OFF — the only fixture that lays a Discount column out with no Tax column next to it, because `totals.taxes` is empty. That combination matters because the two conditional columns are adjacent in the header and a mistake in one arm reads as a mistake in the other: with Tax present, a Discount bug is easy to mis-attribute. Three rentals in one group with a $12.00 discount against a $48.00 total, so the discount is a quarter of the invoice and any rounding error in the Discount cell is visible at a glance rather than lost in a large figure. It is also the only fixture that renders the `Subtotal after Discount` row in the totals block, which only appears when `totals.discount_amount_cents > 0`. The family's OTHER 8-column shape is Duration + Tax with Discount off, and that is `billing-foreign-country` — measured, not assumed: rendered 2026-08-26, this fixture emits 8 columns and so does that one, while `part-paid` emits 7 (it has tax but no rental, so no Duration). A reader who sees only the column count will take one of the two 8-column fixtures for a duplicate of the other; they are not, and neither substitutes. Captured from prod invoice 1996.

fixtures.label: Zero-priced components HIDDEN
fixtures.description: The `hide_zero_priced_components: true` state, and the only fixture in this family that renders it — every other one renders the param's `false` default, so without this the half of the template the param selects is frozen by no golden at all (api-cloudrun#608). Deliberately the SAME source document as `zero-priced-flat-tax` (prod invoice 2390), so the two goldens differ only by the param and the diff between them IS the param's effect. It renders the arithmetic that fixture's own description predicts: the zero-priced child hides and its $12.00 rolls onto the parent, Tax $40.95 -> $52.95 and Total $430.95 -> $442.95, while `#totals` still reads $442.95. This is also the only fixture that exercises the invoice-side predicate at all — the param keys on `zero_priced === true && componentDepth > 0` as of 2026-09-10 (it was a `price.base_cents === 0` proxy before, while the invoice line had no such field), and until this fixture existed that predicate was never rendered in its ON state by anything. Both were re-captured together on 2026-09-06 so the pair stays a controlled comparison on one document.
